text: Lion, a Lisp whose programs are JSON. Numbers, booleans, and `null` are themselves; a string is the value its name is bound to, or else the string; an array is a special form or a call; and a record keeps its keys and evaluates its values. `run` from `@lionlang/core/evaluation/evaluate` evaluates a program in an environment, as an Effect.
The special forms `quote`, `eval`, `begin`, `define`, `lambda`, `cond`, and `match`. A lambda closes over the environment it is made in, and `match` takes a value apart with record patterns.
The standard library, named `module/function`: the `number`, `boolean`, `array`, `string`, `object`, `func`, `value`, and `console` modules.
Host interop. An environment can bind any JavaScript value, object, class, or function, and `object/new`, `object/call-method`, `func/bind`, and `func/callback` work with them.
`packages/agent`, a coding agent written as a Lion program, `agent.json`, that drives a terminal interface and an AI model, with tools to read files and directories.
lionlang.dev, a static site for Lion.

internal: Tooling and tests for the repository: Effect's language service, the compiler settings, relative imports, and tests for the list module.
